hits.text:
I've been actively fighting almost guaranteed age-related loneliness for years, studies show after age 30 you start seeing friends less and when you get older especially men don't have any social life left!

It's preventable, but it takes effort and initiative

We've now organized 70 weekly coworking days where we meet with friends and work together, do show and tell, and try help each other make things (also hardware stuff more recently)

We've also started organizing movie nights, art nights, barbecues, we watched the World Cup final on a projector screen in the garden with friends

We did a collage night the other day where we bought cheap gossip magazines, colored paper, and Pritt glue, and gave everyone scissors to make their own art, I think nobody spent time on their phone for at least 4 hours, making things puts you in a flow state and it's fun to do it in a group because you talk about different stuff while making things than you would for ex having a dinner

Movie nights are nice too but less popular I think cause everyone prefers to watch movies alone and also you can't really talk during a movie

Coworkings range from having sometimes 20 people to sometimes just 2 people, people have their own lives, but me and 
@rameerez
 still try to organize them weekly

One thing I realized is that we are usually the ones organizing stuff, but that's not a bad thing, there's even studies about this, there's usually a few people in a group who organize most of the events

If nobody in your group organizes stuff, it doesn't mean nobody wants to do stuff, but you have to take the initiative to bring people together which isn't easy in a time where phones and apps and the internet are simply easier and cheaper dopamine than driving to a friends house for a party

You can start with a coworking day, everyone brings their laptop, and you provide WiFi and coffee, then later you can try more types of events

Having an active social life is just as important or in some studies even more important for health than physical fitness

After a nice party I feel tired but satisfied, I had fun and didn't spend time on my phone or computer but instead talked and laughed with friends etc.

We don't drink alcohol with very few exceptions and nor do our friends, so it's mostly just having really nice food and sparkling water or kombucha etc, and we don't really need alcohol, after a few hours it gets fun enough anyway!

So I recommend everyone, take initiative, and organize something and get people together, it'll be fun!
hits.name: @levelsio
hits.hook: I've been actively fighting almost guaranteed age-related loneliness for years, studies show after age 30 you start seeing friends less and when you get older e
hits.draft_en:
70 weekly coworkings beat another year of lonely Slack status.

Pieter's thesis is blunt: after 30, friendship dies unless someone organizes. Phones are cheaper dopamine than driving to a friend's house.

Coworking, collage nights, BBQs without alcohol. Flow from making things together beats dinner small talk.

Most groups wait for "someone" to host. You are that someone. Start with WiFi, coffee, and laptops.

Put one recurring block on the calendar this week. Invite 5. Ship the hang.
hits.video_tip: 10-14s: empty calendar → filled weekly block with faces, caption organize or atrophy.

hits.text:
I literally can't think of a better risk/reward bet right now than building a ChatGPT plugin and getting in front of their 1.2 billion weekly users.

As of yesterday, ChatGPT recommends plugins in the middle of conversations. Millions of questions get asked every day with no plugin to recommend. Each one is an empty slot.

Facebook apps in 2007. iPhone apps in 2008. TikTok in 2019. Every big platform has a few months where distribution is free, and most people miss it.

I saw this firsthand when I lived in SF building venture backed companies. They are sacred times!

If I were starting this week:

1. Find a tool or workflow people already Google for or do by hand every week (PDF to Excel, invoice generator, weekly client reports)
2. Build it as a ChatGPT plugin
3. Write the description using the exact phrases people type into ChatGPT
4. Ship 5 of them and see which ones get picked up
5. Double down on the one with the most traction

In 12 months these slots will be crowded but right now they're pretty empty.

Most people will realize ChatGPT plugins were the biggest free distribution channel of 2026 sometime in 2027.
hits.name: GREG ISENBERG
hits.hook: I literally can't think of a better risk/reward bet right now than building a ChatGPT plugin and getting in front of their 1.2 billion weekly users.
hits.draft_en:
ChatGPT just started recommending plugins mid-conversation to 1.2B weekly users. Empty slots are free distribution.

Greg's playbook: pick a weekly hand workflow, ship it as a plugin, describe it in the exact phrases people type, launch 5, double down on the winner.

Facebook 2007. iPhone 2008. TikTok 2019. These windows close. Most people notice in 2027.

If you are still building a landing page for a tool people already ask ChatGPT to do, you are late to the wrong surface.

Ship one plugin this week. Steal the query language from real chats. Kill the other four after traction.
hits.video_tip: 10-13s: empty plugin slots filling, caption free distribution / ship 5 keep 1.

hits.draft_en:
Cutting a liability out of the friend group is product hygiene for your life.

Pieter's restaurant story is extreme on purpose. Slow exits happen first. Then the "I LOVE ALCOHOL" public meltdown.

Warnings first. Then the cut. Tribal risk management is not cruelty.

Same rule in startups: keep the person who raises the mean quality, cut the person who raises the mean chaos.

Write your non-negotiables. Enforce them once. Stop re-litigating every party.

hits.text:
My first OBSERVATIONS from Sundar's Gemini 4 Argon announcement:

1. Quantum. Google's quantum researchers gave Argon a key piece of quantum software to shrink, and in minutes it found a version that needs 40% fewer qubits and operations than the best published human solution. 

Quantum computers are useful ONLY once programs fit on the hardware, so this pulls that date closer from the software side, and it also shortens the time banks and governments have to switch to encryption quantum can't break.

2. Data center memory. A team of Argon agents read Google's server data, found waste, and freed over 300 TiB of memory on their own, with up to 1 PiB expected. 

If agents can do this everywhere, companies will point them at their cloud bills before buying more servers, and some of the huge data center buildout may turn out to need less hardware than planned.

3. Rewriting old code. Argon agents are converting Google's old C and C++ code into Rust, a safer language, including an 800K- ine operating system kernel.

There are PLENTY of companies stay with outdated software vendors only because switching is painful, and once rewriting is cheap, that lock in starts to break!

4. Faster than the engineers. On one video decoder, Argon ran 100s of experiments and ended up 2.7x faster than the version Google's own engineers wrote. Speeding up your slowest code used to take a specialist team, and now it's something you can run overnight and pay for based on the savings.

5. Million-token answers. The most a model could write in one answer went from 64K tokens to 1 million, enough for a whole codebase or a full due diligence report.

Obviously, nobody can carefully review that much output, so the bottleneck moves from making things to checking them, and tools that verify AI work become a big market.

6. Two versions of the same model. Vetted security teams get Argon with the cyber safety limits removed, and everyone else gets the restricted one. 

The best defense goes to big trusted organizations first, which leaves smaller companies more exposed and creates demand for services that get them "trusted" status. Gotta think about this more and what it means.

7. Finding bugs faster than anyone can fix them. Wiz used Argon to find a serious security hole in hospital software used worldwide that every earlier model missed. When AI can find holes this fast, the pile of known but unpatched bugs becomes the real risk, and whoever makes patching fast wins.

8. Legal work. On Harvey's legal benchmark Argon scored 19.6%, and every other top model was under 7%, the biggest gap in the whole chart!! 

Harvey, a startup, built that test, and now Google launches on it, so owning the benchmark in your industry gives you leverage over the labs.

9. Promo pricing. It launches at $2 in and $10 out per million tokens, about a 20% ish  of GPT6's price, and then doubles. Startups that set their prices on the promo rate will see margins shrink in a few months, even though everyone assumes AI only gets cheaper.

10. Cheap memory. Reused context is 95% off. Products that keep one big shared knowledge base and reuse it across users will run far cheaper than rivals that resend everything each time.

11. Watching the model. Google seals Argon's test environment before training, watches its reasoning live, can stop it mid task, and asked other labs to keep reasoning readable. 

Companies running their own agents will copy this, and monitoring and permissions for AI agents turns into its own product category.

12. Government first. The US government gets access before the public through a voluntary review. 

DC is pretty much the first customer now, and launch dates start depending on its review, not only on when the model is ready. That's the new normal, I guess since the Fable/Mythos debacle.

I'll share more on Gemini 4 as it comes out on 
@startupideaspod
 

Never a dull moment in AI, isn't it?
hits.name: GREG ISENBERG
hits.hook: My first OBSERVATIONS from Sundar's Gemini 4 Argon announcement:
hits.draft_en:
Twelve Argon takes. Three that change founder math this quarter.

1) Agents already freed 300 TiB of Google memory. Point yours at the cloud bill before you buy more boxes.
2) Output jumped to 1M tokens. The bottleneck is verification, not generation. Sell the check.
3) Intro price is ~20% under GPT-6 then doubles. Promo-rate unit economics are a trap.

Also: quantum code shrink, C/C++→Rust rewrites, 2.7x faster video decoder overnight, cyber-unrestricted for vetted orgs, Harvey legal gap, 95% off reused context, gov review before public.

Pick one wedge. Verification tooling, context-cache products, or migration agents. Not all twelve.

Write the one-sentence bet. Ship a spike before the promo ends.
hits.video_tip: 12-15s: 12 cards collapse to 3, caption cloud bill / verify / price for 2x.

When I play Flight Simulator 2024, and I fly crazy for fun, I get overspeed warnings etc. but I just keep flying (with damage off)

In reality at too high speeds things just start falling off an airplane like here the rudder
hits.name: @levelsio
hits.hook: When I play Flight Simulator 2024, and I fly crazy for fun, I get overspeed warnings etc. but I just keep flying (with damage off)
hits.draft_en:
Flight Sim lets you ignore overspeed with damage off. Reality sheds the rudder.

Same gap in shipping AI products. Demo mode hides the failure modes that eat production.

If your agent only works with guardrails off and retries infinite, you do not have a product. You have a clip.

Turn damage on. Watch what breaks at load. Fix that before the launch thread.

Run one real failure drill this week. Document the first thing that falls off.

I've been actively fighting almost guaranteed age-related loneliness for years, studies show after age 30 you start seeing friends less and when you get older especially men don't have any social life left!

It's preventable, but it takes effort and initiative

We've now organized 70 weekly coworking days where we meet with friends and work together, do show and tell, and try help each other make things (also hardware stuff more recently)

We've also started organizing movie nights, art nights, barbecues, we watched the World Cup final on a projector screen in the garden with friends

We did a collage night the other day where we bought cheap gossip magazines, colored paper, and Pritt glue, and gave everyone scissors to make their own art, I think nobody spent time on their phone for at least 4 hours, making things puts you in a flow state and it's fun to do it in a group because you talk about different stuff while making things than you would for ex having a dinner

Movie nights are nice too but less popular I think cause everyone prefers to watch movies alone and also you can't really talk during a movie

Coworkings range from having sometimes 20 people to sometimes just 2 people, people have their own lives, but me and 
@rameerez
 still try to organize them weekly

One thing I realized is that we are usually the ones organizing stuff, but that's not a bad thing, there's even studies about this, there's usually a few people in a group who organize most of the events

If nobody in your group organizes stuff, it doesn't mean nobody wants to do stuff, but you have to take the initiative to bring people together which isn't easy in a time where phones and apps and the internet are simply easier and cheaper dopamine than driving to a friends house for a party

You can start with a coworking day, everyone brings their laptop, and you provide WiFi and coffee, then later you can try more types of events

Having an active social life is just as important or in some studies even more important for health than physical fitness

After a nice party I feel tired but satisfied, I had fun and didn't spend time on my phone or computer but instead talked and laughed with friends etc.

We don't drink alcohol with very few exceptions and nor do our friends, so it's mostly just having really nice food and sparkling water or kombucha etc, and we don't really need alcohol, after a few hours it gets fun enough anyway!

So I recommend everyone, take initiative, and organize something and get people together, it'll be fun!

virals.text:
I literally can't think of a better risk/reward bet right now than building a ChatGPT plugin and getting in front of their 1.2 billion weekly users.

As of yesterday, ChatGPT recommends plugins in the middle of conversations. Millions of questions get asked every day with no plugin to recommend. Each one is an empty slot.

Facebook apps in 2007. iPhone apps in 2008. TikTok in 2019. Every big platform has a few months where distribution is free, and most people miss it.

I saw this firsthand when I lived in SF building venture backed companies. They are sacred times!

If I were starting this week:

1. Find a tool or workflow people already Google for or do by hand every week (PDF to Excel, invoice generator, weekly client reports)
2. Build it as a ChatGPT plugin
3. Write the description using the exact phrases people type into ChatGPT
4. Ship 5 of them and see which ones get picked up
5. Double down on the one with the most traction

In 12 months these slots will be crowded but right now they're pretty empty.

Most people will realize ChatGPT plugins were the biggest free distribution channel of 2026 sometime in 2027.

virals.text:
My first OBSERVATIONS from Sundar's Gemini 4 Argon announcement:

1. Quantum. Google's quantum researchers gave Argon a key piece of quantum software to shrink, and in minutes it found a version that needs 40% fewer qubits and operations than the best published human solution. 

Quantum computers are useful ONLY once programs fit on the hardware, so this pulls that date closer from the software side, and it also shortens the time banks and governments have to switch to encryption quantum can't break.

2. Data center memory. A team of Argon agents read Google's server data, found waste, and freed over 300 TiB of memory on their own, with up to 1 PiB expected. 

If agents can do this everywhere, companies will point them at their cloud bills before buying more servers, and some of the huge data center buildout may turn out to need less hardware than planned.

3. Rewriting old code. Argon agents are converting Google's old C and C++ code into Rust, a safer language, including an 800K- ine operating system kernel.

There are PLENTY of companies stay with outdated software vendors only because switching is painful, and once rewriting is cheap, that lock in starts to break!

4. Faster than the engineers. On one video decoder, Argon ran 100s of experiments and ended up 2.7x faster than the version Google's own engineers wrote. Speeding up your slowest code used to take a specialist team, and now it's something you can run overnight and pay for based on the savings.

5. Million-token answers. The most a model could write in one answer went from 64K tokens to 1 million, enough for a whole codebase or a full due diligence report.

Obviously, nobody can carefully review that much output, so the bottleneck moves from making things to checking them, and tools that verify AI work become a big market.

6. Two versions of the same model. Vetted security teams get Argon with the cyber safety limits removed, and everyone else gets the restricted one. 

The best defense goes to big trusted organizations first, which leaves smaller companies more exposed and creates demand for services that get them "trusted" status. Gotta think about this more and what it means.

7. Finding bugs faster than anyone can fix them. Wiz used Argon to find a serious security hole in hospital software used worldwide that every earlier model missed. When AI can find holes this fast, the pile of known but unpatched bugs becomes the real risk, and whoever makes patching fast wins.

8. Legal work. On Harvey's legal benchmark Argon scored 19.6%, and every other top model was under 7%, the biggest gap in the whole chart!! 

Harvey, a startup, built that test, and now Google launches on it, so owning the benchmark in your industry gives you leverage over the labs.

9. Promo pricing. It launches at $2 in and $10 out per million tokens, about a 20% ish  of GPT6's price, and then doubles. Startups that set their prices on the promo rate will see margins shrink in a few months, even though everyone assumes AI only gets cheaper.

10. Cheap memory. Reused context is 95% off. Products that keep one big shared knowledge base and reuse it across users will run far cheaper than rivals that resend everything each time.

11. Watching the model. Google seals Argon's test environment before training, watches its reasoning live, can stop it mid task, and asked other labs to keep reasoning readable. 

Companies running their own agents will copy this, and monitoring and permissions for AI agents turns into its own product category.

12. Government first. The US government gets access before the public through a voluntary review. 

DC is pretty much the first customer now, and launch dates start depending on its review, not only on when the model is ready. That's the new normal, I guess since the Fable/Mythos debacle.

I'll share more on Gemini 4 as it comes out on 
@startupideaspod
 

Never a dull moment in AI, isn't it?

drafts.draft_en:
ChatGPT is recommending plugins mid-chat to 1.2B weekly users. Most slots are still empty.

That is Facebook apps 2007 energy. Free distribution with a timer.

Build the tool people already type into ChatGPT by hand. PDF to Excel. Invoice packs. Weekly client reports. Describe it in their words.

Ship five thin plugins. Kill four. Scale the one that gets recommended.

Do not wait for the 2027 thinkpiece that says you missed it.
drafts.video_tip: 10-13s: chat bubble → empty plugin slots lighting up, caption ship 5 / keep 1.

drafts.draft_en:
Argon launches at $2 in / $10 out, then the promo ends and the meter roughly doubles.

Founders who model runway on intro tokens will feel a silent margin tax in a quarter.

Same movie as every cloud credit binge. The launch price is marketing. The renewal price is the product.

Build unit economics on the adult rate. Treat intro as a spike budget, not a plan.

Reprice one feature this week assuming 2x token cost. If it still works, you are safe.
drafts.video_tip: 9-12s: $2/$10 badge flipping to 2x, caption intro is bait / model the adult rate.

drafts.draft_en:
Models can now dump a million tokens in one answer. Nobody can carefully read that.

Generation got cheap. Checking got scarce. That is the new market.

Sell verifiers, eval harnesses, and human-in-the-loop gates. Or bolt them onto your own agent before you trust it with money.

If your roadmap is only "more output," you are racing to the wrong scarcity.

Ship one automated check on your highest-risk agent path this week.
drafts.video_tip: 10-12s: wall of tokens → red/green verify stamps, caption check > generate.

drafts.draft_en:
Google's Argon agents read server data and freed 300+ TiB of memory on their own. Up to 1 PiB expected.

Before you buy another GPU reservation, point an agent at your actual cloud waste.

Cost-cutting agents might shrink the hardware boom stories more than another model drop.

Operators who automate FinOps early keep runway. Operators who only ship features burn it.

Run one overnight waste scan on staging. Post the dollars found.
drafts.video_tip: 9-12s: cloud bill bars shrinking overnight, caption agents before more boxes.

drafts.draft_en:
Loneliness after 30 is not fate. It is a calendar with zero hosts.

Pieter ran 70 weekly coworkings plus movie nights and collage sessions. Someone has to send the invite.

Phones are cheaper dopamine than driving to a friend's house. That is why initiative is the scarce skill.

Builders who only ship products and never ship hangs end up rich and alone. Bad trade.

Put a recurring cowork block on the calendar. WiFi, coffee, five people. Do not cancel week one.
drafts.video_tip: 10-14s: solo phone scroll → table of laptops, caption host the hang / compound friends.
